TN-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. Lee term-limited): Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R) won the Aug 6 primary 43.8% to 32.6% over Rep. John Rose; Memphis City Council member Jerri Green (D) won the Democratic primary the same night. Tennessee is guaranteed its first female governor.

candidates.name: Marsha Blackburn
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2019 after 16 years representing Tennessee's 7th District in the House; former state senator and owner of a promotion-event management firm. Raised $10.8 million and won the Aug 6 Republican gubernatorial primary 43.8% to 32.6% over Rep. John Rose.
priorities: Cutting taxes to bolster the economy

health.label: 'Tennesseans know the false promises of a government-controlled system'; wants 'a patient-centered system where families and doctors can make their decisions' (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: 'Secure the border to stem the flow of illegal immigration', deport those who commit crimes, stop sanctuary cities (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Pledges to 'maintain President Trump's tax cuts' and a tax code that is 'simple, fair, low, and permanent' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: 'Expanding school choice, increasing charter school options, making homeschooling easier'; campaign vows to fight 'woke anti-American curriculum' (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Law enforcement 'don't need the federal government to tell them how to do their jobs'; pledges resources to help them keep Tennesseans safe (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: '100 percent pro-life' and 'has always fought to ban late term abortions'; campaign plank on 'defending the innocent right to life' (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Campaign plank on 'Protecting Tennessee Elections And Supporting Party Registration' (campaign issues)

nullNotes.cost: checked Ballotpedia and campaign issues page; 'cutting taxes to bolster our economy' is scored on the taxes axis and no separate price or cost-of-living mechanism is documented
nullNotes.housing: checked Ballotpedia and the campaign issues list; nothing documented
nullNotes.climate: checked Ballotpedia and the campaign issues list; only a 2012-era statement supporting Clean Water Act goals is documented, which does not fit the clean-energy versus expand-all-sources axis

candidates.name: Jerri Green
candidates.background: Memphis City Council member since 2024, former public defender, and community-engagement director at Memphis's Community Legal Center; Georgetown Law graduate who has worked across Tennessee's judicial, legislative, and executive branches. Calls herself 'One Tough Mother.' Won the Aug 6 Democratic primary over four opponents.
priorities: Expand Medicaid and keep rural hospitals open

cost.label: $50 million in TANF funds to clear the childcare waitlist 'for every family' and expand paid family leave (campaign policy agenda)

health.label: 'Expand Medicaid to cover more working families and keep rural hospitals open'; calls healthcare access a right every citizen should have (campaign policy agenda)

housing.label: Use TANF funds to 'waive security deposits and ensure affordable housing for 100,000+ Tennessee families' (campaign policy agenda)

immigration.label: 'Stop the cooperation between the Tennessee Highway Patrol and ICE to protect our immigrant neighbors'; legal representation in deportation cases (campaign policy agenda)

taxes.label: Fund initiatives by 'closing corporate loopholes' and ending voucher spending, without raising taxes on working families (campaign policy agenda)

climate.label: 'Protect Tennessee's rivers, forests, farmland, and public lands from pollution' and invest in renewable energy (campaign policy agenda)

education.label: 'Fully fund K-12 public education, not siphon dollars into unaccountable voucher schemes'; raise teacher pay (campaign policy agenda)

repro.label: 'Repeal Tennessee's near-total abortion ban' and restore access including contraception and emergency care (campaign policy agenda)

nullNotes.safety: her documented public-safety items (universal background checks, red flag laws) are gun measures, which are excluded from this axis by policy; no non-gun policing or sentencing stance found on campaign policy agenda, Ballotpedia, or WSMV coverage
nullNotes.democracy: campaign mentions 'greater government transparency' but no voting-access or election-rules stance documented on campaign policy agenda, Ballotpedia, or news coverage fetched
